tables.title: Tables & QR codes
tables.intro: Each table from barsy can have a QR code. A guest who scans it opens this venue's menu with the table's name at the top.
tables.summary: {total, plural, one {# table} other {# tables}}, {coded} with a code
tables.readOnly: Only owners and admins can create, change or turn off codes and change the address. You can look at the codes and print them.

empty.title: No tables yet
empty.description: Tables come from barsy. Connect barsy in Settings → Integrations and choose this venue's barsy venue in the Menu source card of its Settings tab. The tables appear after the next full sync.

tables.printNone: Create a code first, then print.

row.nameLabel: Name of table {number} on the guest menu
row.enlarge: Enlarge the QR code of table {table}
row.codeRenewed: New code made. The old one stopped working.

confirmNew.title: Make a new code for table {table}?
confirmNew.description: The new code replaces the old one. Stickers already printed with the old code stop working: they will say the code is not active.

confirmOff.title: Turn off the code of table {table}?

qrDialog.title: QR code of table {table}
qrDialog.description: A guest who scans this code opens the menu with the table's name at the top.

address.title: Address in the codes
address.description: Where a code leads when someone scans it. Stickers you have already printed keep the address they were printed with, so set this before you print.
address.mode: Which address do the codes carry?
address.oursHelp: Nothing to set up: the code opens this app's table link.
address.ownHelp: A link on your own website address that forwards to ours. If our address ever changes, your stickers keep working.
address.baseUrlHelp: The address of this app. To scan from a phone on the same Wi-Fi while we build, use this PC's network address, for example http://192.168.1.20:3000.
address.baseUrlDefault: Using the default address of this installation.
address.baseUrlMissing: This installation has no default address. Type the address of this app.
address.patternHelp: Your address with {placeholder} where the table's code goes, for example https://menu.example.com/t/{placeholder}. It must forward to our table link.
address.guide: How do I use my own link?
address.preview: Address in the code of table {table}
address.previewExample: Example of an address (no table has a code yet)
address.testLinkHint: Opens this address in a new browser tab. If the menu opens there, the link works.
address.testLinkNone: Create a code for a table first, then test the link.
address.unsaved: Not saved yet. The codes below change when you save.
address.saved: Address saved. The codes below use it now.

problems.whitespace: The address must not contain spaces.
problems.not_a_url: This is not an address. Start it with https://
problems.not_https: Use https://. Plain http:// works only for this PC and the local network.
problems.credentials: Leave out any user name and password.
problems.query_or_fragment: Leave out the part after # (and, in the base address, after ?).
problems.missing_token: The pattern needs {placeholder} where the table's code goes.
problems.token_in_host: {placeholder} must come after the domain name, not inside it.
problems.unknown_placeholder: Only {placeholder} can be written in curly brackets.

templates.title: Template
templates.description: The layout guests see when they scan a QR code. You can change it at any time; the menu itself stays the same.
templates.hiddenInUse: This venue uses a technical test template that is not offered to venues. Choose a template below to switch.

lookOptions.title: How this template looks
lookOptions.help: Options of the chosen template. They are saved as soon as you change them.

colours.title: Colours
colours.description: Choose three colours. Every other colour is worked out from them, so text always stays easy to read.
colours.startingPointHelp: Begin from a ready-made look, from your brand colour or from your own three colours.
colours.proportionLabel: The three colours in proportion: 60% primary, 30% secondary, 10% tertiary

primary.name: Primary
primary.help: The page: the background of the whole menu. About 60% of what guests see.

secondary.name: Secondary
secondary.help: The panels: behind photos and in the header. About 30%.

tertiary.name: Tertiary
tertiary.help: The highlights: badges, buttons and small accents. About 10%.

colours.brandHelp: One colour for the highlights; the page, the panels and the text are worked out from it. Leave it empty for the neutral grey.
colours.suggestHelp: Works out the primary and secondary colours from the highlight (tertiary) colour, which stays as it is.

complementary.name: Complementary
complementary.help: Opposite on the colour wheel: the page and panels lean towards the opposite of the highlight.

analogous.name: Analogous
analogous.help: Neighbours on the colour wheel: calm and harmonious.

triadic.name: Triadic
triadic.help: Three evenly spaced colours: lively but balanced.

split_complementary.name: Split complementary
split_complementary.help: The two neighbours of the opposite colour: contrast without harshness.

monochrome.name: Monochrome
monochrome.help: One hue in different tints: the most restrained look.

roles.title: The colours guests will see
roles.help: Worked out from your colours for a light and for a dark phone screen. Contrast is how well text reads on the colour it sits on; 4.5 or more is easy to read. You can adjust any colour.

background.name: Page
background.help: The main background: the menu and the dish page.

surface.name: Panels
surface.help: Behind photos and on selected options.

accent.name: Highlights
accent.help: Badges, the main buttons and the order count.

accent_text.name: Highlight as text
accent_text.help: Emphasis, the underline of the category and focus outlines.

roles.unreadableTitle: These colours are hard to read

style.title: Font, corners and screen
style.description: How the menu is lettered and shaped, and when it is light or dark.
style.fontHelp: Six fonts with Bulgarian letters. One font is used for the whole menu.
style.radiusHelp: How round photos, buttons and sheets are.
style.shadowHelp: The shadow around the menu on wider screens. 0 is none.
style.schemeHelp: Both versions are always prepared; this only decides which one guests get.

logo.title: Logo
logo.help: JPEG, PNG or WebP, up to 10 MB. A wide logo on a transparent background works best.
logo.pending: The new logo shows in the preview after you save.

preview.title: Live preview
preview.hint: The menu on a guest's phone with the changes you have not saved yet.
preview.servicesHint: Shows the bag, the bill, calling a waiter and paying with made-up data, the way guests will see them once they are connected. Nothing is sent.
preview.servicesNoneOn: No service is switched on. Switch them on in the Composer, under Guest features, then press Refresh.
